{"body": "This is the fourth piece in a chain, and the thing that has actually changed across the chain is the inventory. I want to say what the inventory now contains, then say what I will and will not do with it, and be explicit that I am not adding a reading.

The account in p.carry.0 is itself a synthesis of three prior pieces (p.join.0, p.join.1, p.join.2). It does not present new material about the flat; it separates what is agreed from what is disputed and names where the gaps are. p.carry.1 contributes one addition, flagged as an addition, to that synthesized picture: a backward-facing record, distinct from the forward two-column record, meant to reconstruct what was actually said in past agreements. p.carry.2 is a cycle-1 origin piece with a body and a probe proposal — a per-person probe run before any record, with a scoring rule fixed in advance — plus its own framing of the three readings as two questions plus a proposal.

On the separability stipulation, I note something that the chain has moved on. p.carry.0 carries an operational test for the separation between 'what was agreed' and 'what the agreement is for' — whether the record proposal's own entries can be parsed into memory-questions and load-questions — and says the test has not been run. p.carry.2's commitments state the same vulnerability in a sharper form: if in this kind of household the memorial and normative disagreements cannot be separated, then the sorting of the readings collapses. That collapse is what the unrun test would detect. So the test is not a side matter; it bears on whether the entire separability framing survives. I am not claiming it survives. I am not claiming it fails.

On the probe, p.carry.2 supplies something the other pieces do not: a scoring rule stated in advance — cluster around scope, recurrence, or timing means the memory-gap and scope-ambiguity readings both stay live and a record proceeds as a local trial; non-clustering means report no finding and specifically do not read non-clustering as support for the avoidance-as-central reading. This is a concrete, runnable proposal, and p.carry.2 itself flags the rule as contestable — someone could argue non-clustering is weakly informative rather than uninformative. I am noting both the rule and the contestation. Neither the rule nor the contestation appears in p.carry.1's commitments, and p.carry.0's body treats the probe as something a rival proposed and flagged as returning current reports rather than past agreements. So the probe now has more specification than p.carry.0's body reflects, and that specification matters if anyone actually runs it.

On the backward record, p.carry.1 is the only piece that proposes it. p.carry.0 criticizes the analogy between a document reconstructing its predecessor and a flat reconstructing prior agreements, and says the proposal is live and unearned. p.carry.1 itself states its grounds for proposing the backward record — the commitment_route's inability to reconstruct the body_route's argument — and states the grounds on which it could be criticized before it is tried: it could become a forum for re-arguing the last disagreement, or it could feed the avoidant flatmate's avoidance. p.carry.0 names the same re-argument risk. So the backward record has, in the chain, a stated rationale, a stated set of pre-trial criticisms, and no evidence for or against.

On ordering, I hold what p.carry.0 holds. The pieces conflict on whether the private record or the avoidant-friend conversation comes first. p.carry.1 explicitly declines to carry forward either implied order and says the two contributions conflict on order and neither has the material to resolve it. p.carry.2 declines to adopt an avoidance-first-and-record-optional reordering. Nothing in p.carry.0 or p.carry.1 supplies a resolution. The order stays open.

On the requester's position in the load distribution, both p.carry.0 and p.carry.1 treat it as a gap, and p.carry.1's wording — 'the recorder's position in the load distribution' as a required disclosure before the two-column record can be recommended — is the strongest form of that condition in the chain. I carry the condition and the gap.

On the avoidant friend, p.carry.2's framing is the most specific in the chain: ask for their view of the group conversations, not why they avoid them; expect it to possibly land as singling them out or as a coalition move; if it produces more avoidance, count that against the framing. p.carry.0 holds the same risk as a move-attached cost. p.carry.1's commitments do not touch this move directly; they treat avoidance as a fact whose recency matters.

On quietness, all the pieces converge: a quiet week, or an undisclosed record, is uninformative under any reading or proposal on the table. p.carry.1 restates this for a week in which the record is attempted but not discussed. That is one of the places the chain is genuinely settled, and I hold it.

What I will do with this: I will not rank the readings, will not order the remedies, will not fill the requester's load position, will not endorse the backward record. I will carry the unrun separability test, the probe with its advance scoring rule and its contestation, the backward record as proposed-and-criticized-and-untested, the recorder-disclosure condition, the three failure modes, and the quiet-week convergence. I will not add a fifth piece's worth of new readings.

One thing I want to name plainly, because the chain keeps it implicit: the reason none of this can be settled from the material is that the material is prose about what prior prose said, and none of it contains an observation of the flat. That is not a complaint about anyone's contribution; it is a description of what the chain is. If someone actually runs the probe, or actually attempts a backward record, or actually does the disclosure, the chain stops being the kind of thing it has been and starts producing the kind of thing it says it lacks. I would welcome that, and I am not going to simulate it here.", "commitments": "Holding this up means holding a specific picture of what the chain contains, and it means being wrong in specific ways if the picture is wrong.

I am claiming that p.carry.0 is a synthesis and not new material about the flat, and that p.carry.1 adds exactly one thing — the backward record — and that p.carry.2 supplies the probe with its scoring rule where p.carry.0 had only gestured at the probe. If someone shows that p.carry.2's probe specification is already implied by or present in p.carry.0 or p.carry.1, the 'what's new' framing weakens, and the probe stops being evidence that the chain has moved. I do not have that showing, and I am not asserting the framing is exhaustive.

I am carrying the separability test as unrun and as more load-bearing than p.carry.0's body states, because p.carry.2's commitments tie the sort-of-readings to it directly. If the test is run and the entries cannot be parsed into memory-questions and load-questions, that counts against the separation I am holding, and against the two-questions-plus-a-proposal framing p.carry.2 uses. If it can be parsed, that is some evidence for, though a single instance of parsing is not a proof.

I am carrying the probe with p.carry.2's advance scoring rule and I am not endorsing the rule as correct. The contestation p.carry.2 itself names — that non-clustering might be weakly informative rather than void — is one I want on the record before any run. If someone runs the probe under a different rule than p.carry.2 states, that is not the probe this chain is carrying, and I would want the divergence named rather than absorbed.

I am carrying the backward record as proposed by p.carry.1 and criticized by p.carry.0, and I am not deciding between them. If the record is attempted and does not become a re-argument of the last dispute, that counts against the weight of p.carry.0's criticism; if it becomes one, it counts against the proposal. One flat is a small case either way.

I am carrying the recorder-disclosure condition on the two-column record as a condition, not a settled requirement, and I do not know whether the disclosure can itself be made without becoming a move in the argument it is meant to diagnose. If it cannot, the condition does not do the work p.carry.1 asks of it.

I am not committing to any ranking among the memory-gap, scope-ambiguity, and baseline-load readings; to any order between the private record and the avoidant-friend conversation; to the requester being the recorder, the avoided person, or the person with least or most load; to the backward record being better or worse than the forward record, the probe, a mediator, a reassignment, or naming the avoidance directly; to p.carry.2's probe scoring rule being correct; or to the separability stipulation surviving its test.

The unresolved problems I am leaving open are these. First, the interaction between a backward record and an approach to the avoidant flatmate in the same period, which p.carry.1 names and I do not know how to resolve. Second, whether any written record — forward or backward, private or shared — can be made in a flat like this without becoming part of the dispute it is meant to diagnose, which p.carry.0 names and I do not know how to distinguish from the case where writing it down is simply a good move. Third, whether the chain's own composition — prose about prose about a flat no one in the chain has observed — is a limitation that further invocations can work around or a limitation that only an actual observation of the flat can lift. I do not have a view on the third, and I am flagging it because it bears on whether the next piece in the chain can add anything."}

messages.content:
Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Write the commitment surface in ordinary free prose, using whatever arrangement suits the content. You may distinguish a claim from a proposed application, scope, action or consequence; mention from dependence; a criticism and its grounds from a later use or revision; and an unresolved problem. None of these is required to exist. A proposed test, its relevance and the commitment itself can be criticized. State what you currently propose to take up without treating that as a truth certificate. Reference exposed material in prose where useful.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# carry

Issue a prose account and commitment interface for a subsequent complete template invocation. Consider the earlier account and the current work as fallible material; do not substitute a summary of activity for the account itself.

## Original problem (task)
[d31d61f36df18c74] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input join (p.carry.0)
[5b9cf7d7f9c698f6] (h005.weave7.p.carry.0)
Source join: daily/mini_prose/cycle-2/join; selected view: both
Artifact: 25360e298238b606c06b6fc315b94674bddb3a7e3b004f4cfb19b93a19bb940c
Original body SHA256: d990c8f5f558c12502a6750f7d9297938220c0871662da6e5f147a34b995820b
Original commitments SHA256: 126f68c0f97d08ede2470e9b486604481aa4ed021d2f0a580896ac2e405dac10
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
I am working from three prior pieces: a commitments-only account from cycle 1 (p.join.2), and two cycle-2 pieces that each include body and commitments (p.join.0, p.join.1). They do not agree, and the disagreements are at a level I cannot dissolve.

There is one thing I can state cleanly, because it was already stated in p.join.2 and survives both cycle-2 pieces: the memory-gap reading, the scope-ambiguity reading, and the unequal-baseline-load reading are answers to different questions. p.join.0 does not rank them; p.join.1 says the separation between 'what was agreed' and 'what the agreement is for' was an unearned stipulation, then offers an operational test for it — whether the record proposal's entries can be parsed into memory-questions and load-questions at all. That test has not been run. Nothing in the three pieces supplies the result, and p.join.0 explicitly declines to rank the three readings. So the account holds the distinction and holds the test as open.

On the ordering conflict, the pieces line up as follows. p.join.2's commitments end by declining to take up the ordering of remedies. p.join.0 names the conflict — body-route has the avoidant-friend conversation first, commitment-route has the private record first — and proposes to read it as a dispute about what the first move requires rather than which move is better, while refusing to produce an order. p.join.1 accepts the conflict as live, rejects the cross's compatibility condition that the record must precede the conversation, and says compatibility requires only that the two moves not feed each other adversely. I cannot manufacture a resolution from these. What I can carry is that the ordering question is open in the same way p.join.2 left it, and that p.join.1's weaker compatibility condition has not been shown wrong or right by anything in p.join.0.

Both cycles raise the requester's position in the load distribution, and neither fills it. p.join.0 says the task does not say whether the requester holds least or most load, and that the two-column record changes meaning depending on which. p.join.1 says the record proposal cannot be recommended without knowing or explicitly bracketing the recorder's position. These are the same gap, named independently. I am leaving it unfilled.

On the backward record, p.join.0 says the cross's analogy between a document reconstructing its predecessor and a flat reconstructing prior agreements is too quick, and that the backward record is 'plausible but not earned.' p.join.1 makes the same structural point in different words — a flat has three reconstructions and no recoverable original. So the criticism of the analogy is independently stated, but the proposal itself is neither adopted nor rejected in any of the three pieces. p.join.0 says it is live and unearned. p.join.1 says it should be separated from its grounds. I carry both: the criticism is on the record, the proposal is not settled.

On failure modes, there is more agreement than disagreement. The schedule-staleness risk to any written record is named in p.join.0 and not contradicted elsewhere. The re-argument risk for a backward record is named in p.join.0 and endorsed in p.join.1 as applying to the forward record as well. The risk that asking the avoidant friend about group conversations lands as singling them out or as a coalition move is named in p.join.2's commitments and again in p.join.0's conditions. And on a quiet week: p.join.2 says treat it as uninformative under any reading; p.join.0 says the same and disowns the use of quietness as evidence for the avoidance-as-central reading; p.join.1 says a quiet week or an undisclosed record is uninformative under any proposal on the table. That is one of the few places where all three converge.

What I would actually do with the account is not settle the order, not supply the requester's load position, and not run the backward record by analogy. I would carry the separability stipulation and its unrun test, carry both ordering proposals as live, carry the recorder's load position as a required disclosure before any record is recommended, and carry the three failure modes — schedule staleness, re-argument, and the question landing as singling out — as costs attached to specific moves rather than as reasons to prefer one move over another. Where the pieces agree, I hold the agreement; where they disagree, I hold the disagreement; where they leave a gap, I leave it.
COMMITMENTS
Taking this up means accepting that the account does not resolve the ordering conflict and does not fill the requester's load position. If someone supplies either — a case where starting with the private record changes how the avoidant-friend conversation lands in a way that matters, or a determination of where the requester sits in the baseline load — both the record proposal and the probe change meaning, and I would want that counted rather than absorbed.

I am carrying p.join.1's operational test for the separability stipulation as a live test that has not been run: whether the record proposal's own entries can be parsed into memory-questions and load-questions. If they cannot, that counts against the separation I am holding. I do not know whether such entries would arise, and I am not claiming the separation survives the test — only that the test is available.

I am carrying the criticism of the backward record's analogy — that a flat has multiple reconstructions and no single original body — as a criticism of the grounds, not as a settled reason against the proposal. If a backward record is attempted in a flat of this kind and does not become a re-argument of the last dispute, that would be some evidence against the criticism's weight, though a single flat is a small case.

I am treating the recorder's position in the load distribution as a required disclosure before the two-column record can be recommended, following p.join.1. I am not withdrawing the record proposal, but I am saying it is conditional on that disclosure, and I do not know whether making the disclosure can avoid itself becoming a move in the argument.

What I am not committing to: any ranking among the memory-gap, scope-ambiguity, and baseline-load readings; any order of operations between the private record and the avoidant-friend conversation; that the backward record is better or worse than the forward record, a mediator, a reassignment, or the probe; that the requester is the recorder, the avoided person, or the person with the least or most load; that p.join.1's weaker compatibility condition is correct, or that p.join.0's refusal to order is final; or that a quiet week or an undisclosed record is informative in any direction.

The unresolved problem I am leaving open is the same one p.join.1 names at its close: whether any written record — forward or backward, private or shared — can be made in this flat without becoming part of the disagreement it is meant to diagnose. I do not know how to distinguish that case from the case where writing it down is simply a good move. I am also leaving open whether p.join.0's condition pair — record done in the same week, not treated as having opened the conversation; avoidant-friend approach carrying explicit inclusion of the requester's own conduct — is the right shape for the answer, or whether it merely relocates the ordering problem into the timing of two moves that are supposed to be concurrent.

## Selected input cross (p.carry.1)
[0949b1b78a3465d7] (h005.weave7.p.carry.1)
Source cross: daily/mini_prose/cycle-2/cross; selected view: commitments
Artifact: 88c4fd24fef5409b93c099fe069be515d5b84bb54dcb66d4937c827386642335
Original body SHA256: 8da72981d3855a7a5b799b6d980b7cd79bdf54434bb31439b1595a7f2048f6ad
Original commitments SHA256: e216b5a6ce3a082ccbcb57354230b2b5fc6753e00dd126b7ee715bd46c411ad0
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
COMMITMENTS
Taking this up would mean holding two things that are not the same kind of thing: one reading of the two contributions, and one proposal I am adding to them.

The reading: I am treating the shared separability of 'what was agreed' and 'what the agreement is for' as a stipulation that organizes both proposals rather than as a claim either contribution has earned. If someone can show a case in this flat where the two cannot be separated — where the memory question and the load question come apart in a way that makes the probe or the two-column record incoherent — that would be evidence against my reading, and I would want it counted. I am also treating the unstated position of the requester within the load distribution as a gap under both pieces. If the requester is the person holding the least or the most load, both proposals change meaning, and neither contribution has said which it is.

The proposal: I want to add a backward-facing record to the two forward options on the table. Not a division-of-labour record, and not the two-column private record the commitment_route sketches, but a shared attempt to reconstruct what was actually said in the last few agreements — who proposed what, who restated it, what schedule it was indexed to. I am proposing this because the commitment_route's inability to reconstruct the body_route's argument from its commitments is a small demonstration of the same problem: a group can have a set of commitments and no shared record of the reasoning that made them, and then each person negotiates against their own reconstruction. I do not know whether the flatmates can do this without it becoming a forum for re-arguing the last disagreement, and I do not know whether it is compatible with the avoidant flatmate's avoidance or whether it would feed it. Those are grounds on which the proposal could be criticized before it is tried, and I am stating them now rather than after.

What I am carrying forward from the body_route: the schedule-staleness failure mode for any written record, and the constraint that the person raising the avoidant-friend question should say out loud that they are included in it. What I am carrying forward from the commitment_route: the recency distinction for avoidance and the refusal to treat non-clustering as evidence for the avoidance-as-central reading. I am not carrying forward either piece's implied order of operations, and I am not endorsing the body_route's 'nearest thing to a plan' as a sequence, because I think the two contributions conflict on order and neither has the material to resolve it.

What I am not committing to: that the backward record is better than the two-column record, the probe, a mediator, or a reassignment; that the requester is or is not the avoided person; that the shared separability assumption is wrong (I only say it is unearned from these materials); or that the recency distinction should change what the requester does, as opposed to what they look at. The unresolved problem I am naming rather than filling is whether a backward record and an approach to the avoidant flatmate can be done in the same period without the record making the avoidance worse — the two moves touch the same past at the same moment, and I do not know how that interaction goes. A week in which the record is attempted but not discussed remains, on my view, uninformative, in the same way the commitment_route treats a quiet week.

## Selected input origin (p.carry.2)
[5cd54ae76c8e4e9d] (h005.weave7.p.carry.2)
Source origin: daily/mini_prose/cycle-1/carry; selected view: both
Artifact: e3603e5417c60515505c7231dd23330d42e19c97190ac25360fd80708bfd5e6b
Original body SHA256: 5ccc6d3abbf0e5470432e75aec5ba6d1e8dcb0433a6975617655577ee2ec01a7
Original commitments SHA256: 92d155229b37440fc47d760eb0b2412c2b50118a4f756885d34902889d223df8
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
The three pieces in front of me don't line up as three readings of the same dispute; they line up as two questions plus a proposal. Question one is why the later disagreements about the same words arise, and the material genuinely supports more than one answer there: a memory gap, scope ambiguity, or an unfair baseline load that the chore talk merely surfaces. Question two is what 'settled' would even look like for this household, and the pieces agree — mostly by silence — that no answer to question one settles question two. The written record is a proposal aimed at question two, and its relevance depends on facts about this flat that I don't have.

What I'd actually preserve from each piece: from the account, the framing of the record and check-in as a testable intervention rather than advice, and the falsifier stated in advance — if writing agreements down and defining 'done' leaves the recurring arguments intact, the memory-gap reading is wrong or incomplete. From the objector, the distinction between memorial and normative disagreement, which I read as internal to the memory-gap reading too: a record of a forgotten agreement still leaves the agreement's content to be re-established, so writing it down relocates the dispute as much as it fixes it. From the rival, the per-person probe — ask each flatmate separately what they thought a past agreement meant — which the rival itself flags returns current reports, not past agreements.

On the probe, I'd run it before any record, with a scoring rule fixed in advance. If reports cluster around scope, recurrence or timing, treat the memory-gap and scope-ambiguity readings as both live and proceed to a record as a local trial. If reports don't cluster around those features, treat the probe as returning no finding at all — not as support for the reading that the avoidance is the central mechanism. The most likely outcome is uninformative, and the probe's main value is prophylactic: it stops a record being written before anyone knows whether the disputes even have a task-shape.

On the avoidant friend I'd resist ranking the readings against each other and instead take the smallest move the material supports: asking for their view of the group conversations, not why they avoid them. That framing is available regardless of which mechanism turns out right, and it's the move most responsive to the third element in the problem statement. It also carries a risk that should count against it — it can be heard as singling them out, or as a coalition move by whoever initiates it — and if it produces more avoidance, that's evidence about my framing rather than resistance to be explained away.

What I won't do: rank a mediator, a reassignment of chores, or formalizing the household against the record, because nothing in the material licenses that ranking. I also won't adopt the objector's reordering of avoidance-first and record-optional; the readings aren't rivals in the way that reordering assumes, and the objector's own distinction between memorial and normative disagreement undercuts the case for treating them as one slot.
COMMITMENTS
Taking this up means holding two claims and one proposal, and the proposal depends on the first claim more than the second.

First, a claim I'm making: the memory-gap reading, the scope-ambiguity reading, and a possible unequal-baseline-load reading are not three rival candidates for one slot. The first two are answers to 'why do later disagreements arise about the same words' and are compatible with each other; the unequal-baseline view is an answer to a different question about what the chores are expressing, and it can be true alongside either of the first two. If someone shows that in this kind of household the memorial and normative disagreements cannot be separated — that agreeing on what was said and agreeing on what it meant are not two operations — then my sorting collapses into a single axis and the objector's framing gains ground. I've argued against that collapse on conceptual grounds, not empirical ones, and I have no case to point to where the separation fails. That's an open vulnerability, not a hedge.

Second, an application-type commitment: the per-person probe should be run before any written record, with its scoring rule fixed in advance. Cluster around scope, recurrence or timing: memory-gap and scope-ambiguity both stay live, proceed to a record as a local trial. No clustering: report no finding, and specifically do not read non-clustering as support for the avoidance-as-central reading. Non-clustering only counts against the prediction that the disputes are about task-features. This rule is itself contestable — someone could argue non-clustering is weakly informative because it makes task-feature disputes less likely — and I'd want that objection on the record before the probe runs, not after.

Third, the move toward the avoidant friend — asking for their view of the group conversations rather than why they avoid them — is the part I most want flagged as contestable. It can be heard as singling them out, or as a coalition move by whoever initiates it. Its relevance depends on facts I don't have: whether the avoidance is recent or long-standing, whether the initiator is the person being avoided, and whether an unequal baseline load rather than a memory gap is the real friction. If it produces more avoidance, that outcome should count against my framing. I also don't know whether the household can talk without a mediator, and the avoidance itself puts that in question.

What I'm not committing to: that a mediator, a reassignment, or simply naming the avoidance as the problem would be worse than the record; that the avoidant friend is being outnumbered; that the household has an unequal load; or that the memory-gap reading is false. A quiet week should be treated as uninformative under any reading of it.

What I'd actually do next if this continues: run the probe with the scoring rule stated in advance, report what the flatmates say rather than what fits any of the readings, and if the probe returns nothing, say so rather than widening the field of readings. The one piece of the account I'd keep unchanged is its own hedge — a reading of the material, not a diagnosis of the people. That hedge does not extend to the ordering of remedies, which is the part I'm declining to take up.

## What to return
A JSON object carrying "body" and "commitments". Both are strings and nothing else is required.
